content.rendered:
“Use your mind to exercise your internal energy.  Let the internal energy sink and be attached to your body.  Eventually, the internal energy can be condensed into the bone marrow.” -Ta’i Chi Classics, Translated by Waysun Liao.

“When we are asleep, the circulation slows down, especially in the legs which are farthest from the heart.  Toxins start to settle in the legs and feet areas.  When activating (the toes) it will help to clear out the toxins that accumulate in the limbs and backs of the knees.”  Rub the toes together 20-30 times on each side.

“Veins are the return routes of the blood to the heart.  The most common places for blood to clot are the veins of the feet.  This can be caused by wearing high heels, wearing tight shoes, or wearing the wrong shoes.  These will tend to harden the veins and slow down the entire foot circulation.” Pull the toes toward you 20-30 time on each side.  -Chi Self Massage, Mantak Chia

Relax the Jaw
Stress overwhelms.
Jaw clenches tightly, teeth grind.
Massage jaw, relax.

34. The Great Tao Does Not Impose
The great Tao is like a flood,
Everything it touches is affected.
It nurtures all things,
Yet controls nothing.

It brings energy to all,
Yet does not impose upon it.
People may think it is small,
Because it does not control.

Yet it is great,
Precisely because,
It is unattached to the outcome.

Knowing oneself is enlightenment.

To overcome another takes power.
To overcome one’s self takes honesty.

Contentment comes when you know
You have enough.
Adhering to the Way
Means staying in the center.

Know yourself, be content,
And stay in the center.

title.rendered: Maintain Clarity of Mind

content.rendered:
“The accomplished ones, of ancient times, advised people how to guard themselves against disease-causing factors. On the mental level, one should remain calm and avoid excessive desires and fantasies, recognizing and maintaining the natural purity and clarity of the mind. When internal energies are able to circulate smoothly and freely, and the energy of the mind is not scattered, but is focused and concentrated, illness and disease can be avoided.”

-The Yellow Emperor’s Classic, ~240 B.C. translated by Maoshing Ni,
Shambala Publications ISBN 1-57062-080-6

 

Man Following Tao as River Flows to the Sea

The Tao is unnamable.
Even though it is simple,
it is below nothing in the world.
If a ruler could merge with it,
the people would be at peace.

If Heaven and Earth could unite in the heart,
All things would be equal.
When everything is equal,
It is easy to find health and longevity.

Man following Tao
is like a river flowing to the sea.

title.rendered: Do Your Work, Then Rest

content.rendered:
If you learn to follow the Tao,
You learn not to force things,
Or engage in senseless arguments.

Every force has a counter-force,
Every “wrong” person wants their turn to be right.
Arguing or violence always activates a counter balance.

The inner alchemist performs
His spiritual practice and then rests.
He doesn’t try to dominate situations
Or rush his spiritual progress.

He doesn’t need to get his way in an argument,
Because he is happy with himself.
Because he is happy with himself,
He does not have to overdo his progress.

To overdo your progress is to go against the Tao.
To go against the Tao is to hasten decay.

title.rendered: How Long Has the Bright Moon Existed?

content.rendered:
How long has the bright moon existed?
I raise the wine cup to ask the sapphire sky
What year is tonight in celestial palaces?
I could ride the wind to return there
but fear the unbearable chill
high in jade towers with jeweled eaves

I dance with my crisp shadow
in delight known only to mortals
Circles painted pavilions
Seeps over carved doors
Shines on the sleepless

The moon has no regrets
Why does it glow in full over parted humans?
Misery and joy cycle as we separate and reunite
The moon wanes and waxes
Time forbids perfection
Let us live long to share moonlight’s spell
though a thousand miles apart

— Su Dongpo, Song poet, 1036-1101 CE

Emulate the mighty river

Know how to shine brightly,
But keep to the darkness.
Emulate the pattern of nature
And the Tao will be strong inside of you.

Know the familiar,
But keep to the unfamiliar;
Accepting things as they are.

When you accept things as they are,
The Tao will shine inside you,
And you’ll return to your original nature.

The diamond emerges from a lump of coal.
The pot is shaped from a mound of clay.
The alchemist turns lead into gold.

To flit about in this manner

What was present before the creation of all things?
Still, silent, unchanging; it was the Mother of all things.

I don’t know its name,
So I will call it Tao.
Tao means great.
Great means far.
Far means far away.
Far away means returning.

The sage can follow this pattern inside himself,
And thus return to the Tao.

title.rendered: Simple Words Can Transmit the Message

content.rendered:
Simple words can transmit the message.
To learn this, study nature.
A fierce tornado won’t last all morning.
Neither does a sudden downpour continue all day.

The Tao is the architect of nature.
If the great Tao cannot make fierce and sudden things last,
What hope does man have of sustaining force and temper?
Therefore, if you merge with nature,
Your actions follow the Tao.

If you open yourself to virtue, virtue will flow through you.
If you allow yourself to yield, you can learn what forcefulness cannot.

Open yourself to natural ways.
Follow the path of the Tao.
Your life will become much easier.

title.rendered: Acknowledge Your Fragments to Become Whole

content.rendered:
Acknowledge your fragments to become whole.
See your crookedness to become straight.
Empty yourself to become full.
Abandon your fear of death to become truly alive.
Give up your possessions to receive what truly matters.
The alchemist sees polarities as points on the same continuum.

Without trying, you can shine brightly for all to see.
By not trying to prove yourself, you become trustworthy.
When you forget who you are, people recognize themselves in you.
When you don’t have to win an argument, you will become happy.

It is not idle chatter that the ancients said
“By acknowledging your fragments, you become whole.”
When you see your flaws, you can heal them.

He can follow it because
He doesn’t try to hold it like a dogma.

If the Tao is dark and vast, how can he be radiant?
He is radiant because the Tao is the source of health.

The Tao was present before creation.
How does the alchemist know this?
He knows by looking inside himself.

content.rendered:
Stop thinking and your problems cease.
What is the difference between good and bad?
Who decides what is right and wrong?
Is it necessary to fear what others fear?

Everyone is running about, trying to get it all done today.
The alchemist is unmoved, like a baby before it learns to smile.
He is waiting, as if there is nowhere to go.

Others try storing up goods;
The alchemist seems simple.
Others want to be bright and flashy;
The alchemist seems dark.
Others have to be on alert;
The alchemist is as calm as the ocean depths.
Others discuss their ways and means;
The alchemist seems unsophisticated.

He is different than others.
He relies on the Tao.

title.rendered: Temporary Defeat v. Failure

content.rendered:
Temporary Defeat v. Failure
Temporary defeat is like encountering a detour on our way to work. Failure is like a car breakdown that prevents us from making it to work at all—and then we quit at the side of the road and our dream of getting to work dies.

Zig Ziglar used to say that “we don’t drown if we fall in water, we only drown if we stay there.” As we encounter setbacks, we need to honestly analyze if this is a temporary defeat that we will learn and grow from, or if this will be the failure that means the end of this particular project, goal, career, or relationship.

We can rebound from temporary defeat, we cannot rebound from failure. We can often choose which it will be.

Allow your thoughts to leave your head.

Being impartial, you see the oneness of all things.
Seeing the oneness of all things, you merge with the Tao.

title.rendered: Can You Yield Until Your Mind is Clear?

content.rendered:
The Taoist masters of old were wise and lived in harmony.
Their minds were deep and they kept their skills hidden.
Because their minds can’t be fathomed and their skills were hidden,
How can we understand them?

They were careful, like one standing on slippery rocks.
They were alert, like a sniper looking through his rifle’s scope.
They were polite, like a visitor in a foreign land.
They flowed like an ancient river.
They were as flexible as the potter’s clay.
They bent like the willow in the storm,
Their minds were as clear as
A mirror reflecting the summer night.

Can you yield, give, and bend until your mind is clear?
Can you exhibit the patience needed,
To allow inner virtue to arise by itself?
One who merges with the Tao
Doesn’t seek to enforce his will.

By letting things take their natural course,
We become like the old masters in modern times.

content.rendered:
Who can see what can’t be seen?
Who can hear what can’t be heard?
Who can feel what can’t be touched?

Through the practice of subtle energy, the alchemist fuses his senses.
Through the fusion of his senses, he grasps the formless.

The Tao is not bright and not dim. It has no beginning and no end.
Chase it and you’ll never catch it. It is elusive, but it is available everywhere.
Merge with it, though, and you move with the present.

You can’t know it, but you can be it.
Live as the Tao lives. This is the way to peace.

title.rendered: Be Content With What you Have

content.rendered:
Gain and loss can both drain our energy.
Hope and regret both steal the present moment.

How do gain and loss both drain our energy?
When you gain, you have to hold on to it.
When you lose, you lament what is gone.

How do hope and regret both steal the present moment?
Hopes for the future can leave us discontented.
Regret is a fool’s errand, as the past can’t be rewritten.

Therefore, the alchemist is content with what he has.
If he thinks of the past, the focus is on lessons learned.

Rather than regret past mistakes,
He can focus on love for others
And forgiveness of self
When thoughts of the past arise.
Keep your mind with your body,
Allow true virtue to arise.

Over-reaching to listen,

Compulsive thinking of past and future
Will drive a person crazy.

An unquenchable desire for more
Will break the heart.

Therefore, the alchemist turns his senses inward.
He feels the ebb and flow of creation
But maintains his center.

Giving, creating, releasing, and loving

Chase after more, better, and different,

title.rendered: A Simple Life Leads to Clarity

content.rendered:
The Tao is like water, nourishing all things.
Water flows in the low places
And always finds its way home.

The alchemist accepts what is discarded
And recycles energy to benefit all.

He lives a simple life,
Therefore his mind is clear.
Because he is not taking,
He is able to give.

He speaks with clarity,
Because he knows himself.
As a leader, he encourages people
To choose their own destiny.

When taking action,
He applies his best gifts,
And then lets go.
By not striving for more,
He is content,
And people feel safe around him.

It has no beginning.

How is nature eternal?
It has no end.
It has no desires,
Therefore it is always present.

The alchemist does not strive,
Thus he is satisfied.
He does not pursue safety and security,
Yet he has all he needs.

Having been birthed by the Tao,

Practicing in the world steals energy.

If you give away your power
To experts, possessions, or thoughts,
Your body will weaken.

If you trade your health for money,

The alchemist leads his life
By emptying his mind,
Filling his belly, decreasing his desires,
And strengthening his bones.

In this way, he loses material possessions,
But he gains his health and peace of mind.
By giving up clever desires,
He doesn’t spend energy
Chasing passing fads.

Practicing non-doing,
He achieves that which really matters.

title.rendered: Thoughts Are Like Geese, Flying over a Lake

Judging yourself causes
Separation between right and wrong.
Right and wrong creates shame or pride
And an inner shadow.

Labeling thoughts, words, or deeds,
As acceptable or unacceptable
Takes one from wholeness and integrity
Into light and darkness.

Therefore, follow the pattern of virtue
Set forth by nature.
Let your heart shine joy and love to all,
Like the Sun towards the Earth.

Watch your judgments, shame,
And pride float by,
Like a lake watches a flock of geese fly over.

In this way, the Sage allows
The coming and going of people, thoughts, and energy
Without grasping, without gain or loss.
Because of this, he is at peace.

Words can help the mind feel at ease,

From the oneness, energy is pure and whole.
Once individuated, it polarizes.
Harmonizing polarity,
The alchemist returns to oneness.
Living in polarity,
There is only struggle.

Oneness and polarity
Come from the same source.
This source is the Tao.
But who can describe the Tao?
Who can name the source of all things?

title.rendered: Nourish Gently, Lead Quietly

content.rendered:
The wise man does not have
To be right or win an argument.
The virtuous man is not interested
In finding fault.

When you know everything,
There is nothing left to learn.
When you have more than you need,
Its presence weighs you down.
Therefore, the sage does not hoard.
He gives freely and always has plenty.
The Tao nourishes gently and
The master leads quietly.

Flow like water,
Reflect like a mirror,
Respond like an echo.

title.rendered: Practice Forgiveness

content.rendered:
Arguments Between People
Can leave bitter resentments.
How can the relationship return
To a healthy state of affairs?

The sage performs his part of the obligation.
He does not demand justice
On the part of the other.

The virtuous take care
Of their responsibilities.
The virtue-less know only
Blaming and fault-finding.

Meanwhile, the Great Tao is impartial.

content.rendered:
Water is the softest and
Most yielding substance.
Thus, it can dissolve the hard and immovable.

The soft dissolves the hard,
That which yields can overcome
That which is immovable.
In this, water has no equal.

But who practices this in life?
The sage takes the low spots and
Thieves don’t trouble him.
He lives a simple life and
His years are beyond measure.

content.rendered:
When the leaders are greedy
The people do not have time for joy.
When people have no money for themselves
They begin to grow restless.
A wise ruler knows to trust the people,
Let them work in joy and
There will be enough for everyone.

content.rendered:
If you no longer fear death,
Is there anything to be afraid of?
Accept the impermanence of things
Savor each moment.
When you resist natural law,
You try to replace the Great Tao.
You don’t have the energy to replace the Great Tao
And you will only end up exhausted.

title.rendered: Do the Tao to Learn It

content.rendered:
When people lose their sense of awe,
Science explains the five sense world.
When they don’t know how to care for themselves,
They turn to doctors to tell them how to act.

The sage observes from a distance.
He doesn’t meddle in peoples affairs.
Yet, like the eternal Tao, he teaches by example.
To learn it, they simply have to do it.

content.rendered:
The Tao is easy to understand
And easy to put into practice.
Yet no one knows it
And no one practices it.

How can you know the Tao?
By looking inside yourself.
How can you grasp the Tao?
By studying the patterns of nature.

Studying the patterns of nature is very rare.
Looking inside oneself is rarer still.
This is why the Tao is mostly unheard of.

title.rendered: The Best Military Strategists Yield

content.rendered:
Military strategists advise
That it is better to be patient
Than to make the first move.

It is better to withdraw a foot
Than to go forward an inch.

This is the art of moving without advancing.
Pulling back without using force.
Facing the fight without engaging the enemy.

Underestimating the enemy will lead to disaster.
When two forces engage in battle,
The one that yields will win.

title.rendered: A Great Warrior Does Not Seek War

content.rendered:
A great warrior does not seek war.
A great fighter remains calm in the battle.
A great winner does not flaunt his victory.
A great leader lifts up the people.
This is the virtue of not striving.
This is how to lead people.
This is the union of man and Tao.

title.rendered: To Help People, Be Humble

content.rendered:
The ocean is bigger than all streams
Because it sits below them.

If you want to help people,
You have to demonstrate humility.
Listen with your whole heart.
Speak like a subordinate.
Give with both hands.
Learn how to follow.

The master is above all the people,
Though no one feels his weight.

title.rendered: A Simple Life is Easiest to Live

content.rendered:
In old times, the sages taught by example.
When you think you know,
You can’t be taught.
When your mind is open,
You can sense the Way for yourself.

To be a leader, forget cleverness and cunning.
A simple life is the easiest to live.
When you are content,
You become an example
Of how to live your true nature.

title.rendered: There is no shortcut to lasting enlightenment

content.rendered:
It is easy to grasp something at rest.
Plans are easy to make in advance.
Trouble can be overcome before it starts.
Set things in order before chaos erupts.

The oak springs from the acorn.
A sky scraper begins with a pile of dirt.
The journey of 1,000 miles begins with a single step.
Rushing to completion can lead to failure.

Only a fool tries to get something for nothing.
There is no shortcut to lasting enlightenment.
Therefore, the sage watches patiently as things unfold.
He is as tranquil on the first mile as on the 1,000th mile.

Unattached to the outcome, he has nothing to lose.
People usually fail when success is just around the corner.
Thus, have enthusiasm at the end just as at the beginning.

Desire to remain desire-less. Do not collect things.
Let go of fixed notions. Come back to what you have lost.
Help things regain their original nature,
But do so without interfering.

title.rendered: Focus on Health Before You’re Sick

content.rendered:
Practice non-doing.
Observe without action.
The biggest problem in the world
Could have been solved when it was small.

Focus on your health
Before you become sick.
Accomplish great tasks
One small action at a time.

The sage is never doing things for greatness,
Yet achieves greatness
Through completing the simple.

If you face difficulties squarely,
You find no difficulty at all.

content.rendered:
A great nation is like a mighty river valley.
People, goods, and services all flow to it.
The more powerful it becomes,
The more humble it must be.

A great nation is like a great man.
He too must become humble and yielding.
When he harms another, he must make it right.

His greatest enemy stares at him in the mirror.
If a man and a nation are centered in the Tao,
They serve the world and nourish people.
They can be a light to all that see them.

content.rendered:
Ruling a small country is like frying a small fish.
You will ruin it with too much fussing and flipping.
Govern your country like the Tao governs creation and
Negative ways cannot harm the people.
If evil has nothing to oppose, it loses its power.
When opposites will no longer harm each other,
Both are in accord with the Tao.

title.rendered: Be Bright, But Not Flashy

content.rendered:
When the leader governs lightly,
The people are at ease.
When the leader governs harshly,
The people become crafty.
The sage is wise, but not cunning.
He is sharp, but not cutting,
He makes is point, but is not demeaning.
He is bright but is not flashy.

title.rendered: Don’t Try to Control

content.rendered:
Lead by example,
Demonstrate by following the Tao.
Don’t try to control.

Let matters govern themselves.
The more rules there are,
The more rules will be broken.
The more guards there are,
The more insecure people will be.

The cleverer the rules try to be,
The stranger things become.

Therefore, the wise leader says:
If I leave people alone,
They will transform themselves.
If I allow quietude,
The people will find regular routines.
If I don’t interfere,
The people will become prosperous.
If I have no desires,
The people will return to simplicity.

title.rendered: Become Like an Infant

content.rendered:
To merge with the Tao
Is to become like an infant.
Their body is soft but full of energy.
They know nothing
Of merging yin and yang inside themselves,
But yet their bodies pulse with original energy.
They can play and laugh all day long,
But never grow tired,
Because they have inner harmony.

Inner harmony is strong and eternal,
And a raging mind is reflective
Of a being a war with himself.

title.rendered: Treat Others as Yourself

content.rendered:
The man that masters grounding
Cannot be uprooted.
When he knows how to find his center,
He cannot float away.

If you cultivate your inner spirit,
Your virtue will shine clearly.
If your virtue shines clearly,
Your family will flourish.
If your family flourishes,
Your village will prosper.
If your village prospers,
Then your nation will be abundant.

Thus, the sage sees others as if he were them.
He treats other families as if it were his family,
He deals with other villages as his village.
And thus all nations are treated the same as his nation.
Follow the Tao, let it flow through you;
The best chance for peace on earth.

title.rendered: Seal Your Senses, Quiet Your Mind

content.rendered:
At the beginning of the Universe
Was the Tao.
Study the Tao and you’ll understand
All that flow from it.

Understand what flows from it,
But remember the Source.
Practice its ways and
You will have harmony.

If your mind races and
You chase desires;
Your heart will not rest.

Seal your senses,
Quiet your mind,
Do not overwork and
You will know peace.

Turn your eyes inward.
Find the light inside of you.
Yield to the natural way and
You will merge with the source of all things.

title.rendered: The Tao Produces, But Not Possesses

content.rendered:
The Tao gives birth to all things.
It nourishes them, teaches them, shapes them,
And guides them to reach their true expression.
Therefore, all things honor the Tao by their existence.
The Tao produces, but not possesses,
It gives to all, but doesn’t take.
Though it guides, it interferes with none.

title.rendered: Keep Your Life in Order

content.rendered:
Be prepared for anything to happen.
The master follows the saying:
“Live each day like it will be the last,
For one day you will be right.”

When you accept that you will die,
You can truly begin to live.
Settle your affairs at the end of each day.
Tie up your loose ends before bed each night.
Keep your life in order
So you do not leave a mess behind.

The sage is ready for death,
As he is ready for retiring to bed.
He looks back on his life
Like a good day of work.

content.rendered:
The sage’s mind is the mind of nature.
He has no mind of his own.
He accepts the light and the dark.
He accepts the true and the false.
The sage sees creation as a harmonious whole.

title.rendered: Peace is Elusive the Harder You Look For It

content.rendered:
By going inside your body,
You may know the whole world.
By looking at your own soul,
You may see through the windows of heaven.
The further you travel to find peace,
The more elusive it becomes.
Therefore, the sage learns without leaving,
Sees without looking
And all is achieved with non-action.

title.rendered: To Follow the Tao is to be Content

content.rendered:
When a man is in harmony with the Tao,
He cultivates his health and practices virtue.
When a man forgets the about the Tao,
He forgets his health and focuses on selfish desires.
Selfish desires are born from the illusion of fear
He risks falling prey to the curse of discontentedness.
Greed can bring disaster to a man’s health and reputation.
To follow the Tao is know the satisfaction of being content.

Perfecting the spirit seems useless,
But its usefulness is long-lasting.
Filling the body with spirit looks empty,
But it creates health in all aspects.
A life of peace and purpose seems dull,
But it is the most fulfilling way to live.
The greatest skill that is achieved
Passes through all stages of clumsiness.
By allowing things to happen, events take their own course.
By giving up your way, you can discover The Way.

The soft can overcome the hard.
That which has no substance
Can enter where nothing else can.
The sage knows the value of silence.
He practices the power of non-action.

The Tao gave birth to the one.
The one gave birth to heaven and earth.
Heaven and earth gave birth to all things.

All things have yin and yang within them,
The alchemist combines yin and yang
To achieve harmony.

People are reluctant to go within,
Yet this is the very thing that helps
The sage realize the whole universe.

Thus it is true that loses by gaining
And one gains by losing.

title.rendered: Great Music Flows from Simple Notes

content.rendered:
When you hear of the Tao,
You need to immediately practice it.
When normal people hear of the Tao,
They may hold notice it from a distance.
When unconscious people hear of the Tao,
They laugh and dismiss it.

The dismissal by unconscious people
Is what makes it the Tao.
The ancient wisdom says:
“The way to enlightenment looks dark,
Going forward often means going backwards,
An easy path seems hard at first.
The greatest usefulness can often seem useless.
Strength looks like weakness to the untrained eye.
Great music flows from simple notes.”

The Tao is everywhere, but appears nowhere.
It is the foundation of all things, yet very few ever find it.

title.rendered: Let Yourself be Shaped by the Tao

content.rendered:
The natural state of creation is wholeness.
In the natural state, heaven is clear,
The earth is calm, and men fulfill their purpose.
In the natural state, rulers honor the people
And are models for the world.

When creation isn’t in a state of wholeness,
The sky is polluted, the earth is ravaged,
And men live only for themselves.

Therefore, the superior people,
Realize the inferior aspects of themselves.
The high recognize the lowness
From where they came.

The practice of alchemy
Is the journey from fragmentation
Back to wholeness.

Let yourself be shaped by the Tao,
As a jewels form from common stones.

title.rendered: That Which is Lasting Supersedes Passing Fads

content.rendered:
Being virtuous doesn’t require attachment to virtue.
Those without virtue are continuously worried about virtue.

The sage doesn’t focus on doing,
He focuses on being, and thus the right things get done.
The ordinary man is focuses on doing,
Forgets being, and many things are left undone.
The kind, just, and moral men
Could save themselves a lot of trouble
By becoming men of Tao.
When the Tao is lost, man-made kindness,
Righteousness, and morality take its place.

Therefore, the man of Tao focuses
On the inner aspects of life,
Rather than the outer aspects.
He dwells on the substance, not the ornate.
He dwells on the fruit and not the flower.
That which is lasting supersedes passing fads.

content.rendered:
The Tao doesn’t hurry,
But it is always on time.
The alchemist follows the Tao,
And everything is achieved by itself.

Forcing things to change on your time creates desires.
Stabilize your desires and return to the natural flow of time.
When you return to the natural flow of time, all things are at peace.

title.rendered: The Tao is Subtle, but Inexhaustible

content.rendered:
Holding the alchemical image inside,
The sage sees the world as peaceful and calm.
Loud music and bright lights make passing travelers curious,
But, the Tao is so subtle that it is flavorless.
When you look for it, it can’t be seen.
When you listen for it, it can’t be heard.
When you use it, it can’t be exhausted.

title.rendered: The Great Tao Does Not Impose

content.rendered:
The great Tao is like a flood,
Everything it touches is affected.
It nurtures all things,
Yet controls nothing.

It brings energy to all,
Yet does not impose upon it.
People may think it is small,
Because it does not control.

Yet it is great,
Precisely because,
It is unattached to the outcome.

title.rendered: Know Yourself, Be Content, Stay in the Center

content.rendered:
Knowing others is cleverness.
Knowing oneself is enlightenment.

To overcome another takes power.
To overcome one’s self takes honesty.

Contentment comes when you know you have enough.
Adhering to the Tao faithfully requires staying in the center.

Know yourself, be content,
And stay in the center
At the moment of death.
Then your consciousness will live on.

content.rendered:
The Tao is unnameable.
Even though it is simple,
it is below nothing in the world.
If a ruler could merge with it,
the people would be at peace.

When Heaven and Earth unite in the heart
All things are equal.

To know when to stop
Is to find health and longevity.
Man following Tao
is like a river flowing to the sea.

title.rendered: Do Your Work, Then Rest

content.rendered:
If you learn to follow the Tao,
You learn not to force things,
Or engage in senseless arguments.

Every force has a counterforce,
Every “wrong” person wants their turn to be right.
Arguing or violence always activates a counter balance.

The inner alchemist performs
His spiritual practice and then rests.
He doesn’t try to dominate situations
Or rush his spiritual progress.

He doesn’t need to get his way in an argument,
Because he is happy with himself.
Because he is happy with himself,
He does not have to overdo his progress.

To overdo your progress is to go against the Tao.
To go against the Tao is to hasten decay.

If you seek to change the world,
Change yourself instead.
The world is perfect just the way it is,
And doesn’t need our meddling.

Many bounce between fast and slow.
Others bounce between hot and cold.
Some waver between strong and weak.
Others waver between proud and meek.
Save your energy and avoid extremes and excesses.

title.rendered: Emulate the Pattern of Nature

content.rendered:
Know how to be active with your practice,
But rest and recover after.
Emulate the mighty river
Who follows its path spontaneously.

Know how to shine brightly,
But keep to the darkness.
Emulate the pattern of nature
And the Tao will be strong inside of you.

Know the familiar,
But keep to the unfamiliar;
Accepting things as they are.

When you accept things as they are,
The Tao will shine inside you,
And you’ll return to your original nature.

The diamond emerges from a lump of coal.
The pot is shaped from a mound of clay.
The alchemist turns lead into gold.

content.rendered:
To be relaxed in your spiritual journey, be loose about the schedule and destination.
To make your point of view be known, speak softly and listen to others point of view.
In making plans that benefit all, withdraw from calculations and schemes.
Like the sun and the earth, the master is available to all.
Any situation can be a tool for learning and spiritual cultivation.
Recycle what is called bad energy, and use it for the good of all. This is embodying the light.

title.rendered: Find your Center of Gravity

content.rendered:
Find your center of gravity
And you will find lightness.
Find serenity and you will notice
Restlessness before it sets in.

You can travel all day,
Without losing the center of your being.
The sites, no matter how beautiful,
Don’t have to pull you away from your inner awareness.

Many rush around the city,
Chasing this task and that.
To flit about in this manner
Takes away one’s center of gravity.
To chase temporal pleasures leads to restlessness.
Maintain a strong return address
In the center of your being.

title.rendered: Far Away Means Returning

content.rendered:
What was present before the creation of all things?
Still, silent, unchanging; it was the Mother of all things.

I don’t know its name,
So I will call it Tao.
Tao means great.
Great means far.
Far means far away.
Far away means returning.

The sage can follow this pattern inside himself,
And thus return to the Tao.

title.rendered: When You Try to Shine, You Dim Your Light

content.rendered:
When your energy is in your head,
You are ungrounded.
When you hurry,
You are unproductive.
When you try to shine,
You dim your light.
This is like eating too much food, or
A traveler with too much baggage.
To follow the Way is to abstain from overindulgence.

title.rendered: Acknowledge Your Fragments to Become Whole

content.rendered:
Acknowledge your fragments to become whole.
See your crookedness to become straight.
Empty yourself to become full.
Abandon your fear of death to become truly alive.
Give up your possessions to receive what truly matters.
The alchemist sees polarities as points on the same continuum.

Without trying, you can shine brightly for all to see.
By not trying to prove yourself, you become trustworthy.
When you forget who you are, people recognize themselves in you.
When you don’t have to win an argument, you will become happy.

It is not idle chatter that the ancients said
“By acknowledging your fragments, you become whole.”
When you see your flaws, you can heal them.

title.rendered: The Way of Health is to follow the Tao

content.rendered:
The way of health is to follow the Tao.
That is why the alchemist possesses radiance.
How can he follow the Tao, if it is ungraspable?

He can follow it because
He doesn’t try to hold it like a dogma.

If the Tao is dark and vast, how can he be radiant?
He is radiant because the Tao is the source of health.

The Tao was present before creation.
How does the alchemist know this?
He knows by looking inside himself.

title.rendered: Focus on Simplicity, Invest in the Internal

content.rendered:
Forget your mind and your body will be happier.
Forget laws and focus on doing the right thing.
Forget material riches and store up gold inside of you.
The superficial aspects of life should be subordinated,
To focus on simplicity and invest in the internal.

title.rendered: When the Tao is Forgotten, Chaos Emerges

content.rendered:
When you forget the Tao,
You focus only on being a good person.
When you forget to be a good person,
Intelligence becomes the strongest asset.
When intelligence is the strongest asset,
Cleverness and fabrication emerge.
Cleverness and fabrication replace peace.
When there is no peace, chaos emerges.
A state in chaos is taken over by selfish men.

It doesn’t take much–just hearing of someone else’s accomplishments, being criticized, getting into an argument, making a mistake at work–to make us feel that we are not okay. Beginning to understand how our lives have become ensnared in this trance of unworthiness is our first step toward reconnecting with who we really are and what it means to live fully.”

title.rendered: All Things Return to the Tao

content.rendered:
Allow your thoughts to leave your head.
Let your heart forget its desires.
Watch the drama of the world unfold
And contemplate its return to the origin.
All things return to the Tao.
By allowing this process,
You find serenity.
The return to the source creates quietness inside.
The enlightened understand this journey.
This understanding allows tolerance.
Practicing tolerance, you become impartial.
Being impartial, you see the oneness of all things.
Seeing the oneness of all things, you merge with the Tao.
Merging with the Tao, you become eternal.

title.rendered: Can You Yield Until Your Mind is Clear?

content.rendered:
The Taoist masters of old were wise and lived in harmony.
Their minds were deep and they kept their skills hidden.
Because their minds can’t be fathomed and their skills were hidden,
How can we understand them?

They were careful, like one standing on slippery rocks.
They were alert, like a sniper looking through his rifle’s scope.
They were polite, like a visitor in a foreign land.
They flowed like an ancient river.
They were as flexible as the potter’s clay.
They bent like the willow in the storm,
Their minds were as clear as
A mirror reflecting the summer night.

Can you yield, give, and bend until your mind is clear?
Can you exhibit the patience needed
To allow inner virtue to arise by itself?
One who merges with the Tao
Doesn’t seek to enforce his will.
By letting things take their course,
You become like the old masters in modern times.

Book recommendation:

The Total I-Ching, by Stephen Karcher, is a wonderful friend, resources, and provider of perspective for difficult questions in one’s life.  I use it every day.

 

“The I Ching (pronounced ee-ching) is the oldest and most respected oracle or divinatory system in the world. There are currently two translations available which offer somewhat conflicting interpretations – the popular Confucian version and an earlier Taoist version called Zhouyi. Reconstructed by twentieth-century scholars and archaeologists, Zhouyi presents the highly imaginative world of myth and ritual that is the hidden base of thousands of years of Eastern thought.

Now, for the first time ever, Stephen Karcher fuses these two traditions using modern scholarship and archaeological and linguistic research, along with a wide background in Eastern philosophy and comparative religion, and presents them to the modern Western reader in a comprehensive and accessible new form. TOTAL I CHING is a complete oracle with instruction for immediate use in all life situations, but is also the first translation to detail the mythology of the divinatory system, offering a revolutionary new approach to the world’s oldest wisdom tradition.”

title.rendered: Turn Your Senses Inward

content.rendered:
Constantly looking outward,
Exhausts the eyes and liver.
Over-reaching with the ears,
Exhaust the ears and kidneys.
Eating too much numbs the tongue,
And burdens the stomach and spleen.
Compulsive thinking of past and future
Will drive a person crazy.
An unquenchable desire for more
Will break the heart.
Therefore, the alchemist turns his senses inward.
He feels the ebb and flow of creation but maintains his center.

The skin, the hair, and the nails give us our beauty
But the inner essence makes the body move.
The bones are known for their hard and lasting nature,
But the marrow inside gives them their life.
Exercise makes the muscles strong and appealing,
But the quality of chi is the quality of life.
The world focuses on the outside,
But the alchemist cultivates the inside.

title.rendered: Give While Being Unattached to the Outcome

content.rendered:
Can your body, soul, and personality
Function as one?
Will you practice ancient wisdom
And rejuvenate your body?
Growing the good inside you,
Can you purify all the bad?
In your personal relationships,
Can you approach them with love and compassion?
Can you deal with the most important events
By allowing them to find their own path?
Connecting clearly with nature,
Will you release your ego to see the truth in all things?
Giving, creating, releasing, and loving
While being unattached to the outcome;
This is the supreme virtue.

title.rendered: Know When You Have Enough, then Relax

content.rendered:
When you are over-doing,
You become exhausted.
Continue fussing over your work,
And you will spoil it.
Chase after more, better, and different,
You will never relax.
By seeking people’s approval,
It is never found.
Know when you have enough, relax.
This is the only way to peace.

Product Recommendation:

The Emerald Tablet, by Dennis William Hauck is a very exciting page turner, in my opinion, that covers the whole of written history and the spiritual teachings that have spanned that history and guided the leaders of civilization.

Product description:  “The Emerald Tablet is an ancient document that contains the essence of the alchemical teachings that have had an important influence on many Western spiritual and religious traditions. Ostensibly concerned with turning base metals into gold, alchemy was in fact dedicated to transforming the lead of self into the gold of spirit. This brilliant history of alchemy traces its sources back to ancient Egypt, and presents alchemy as a useful, practical system of self-transformation. Each of the seven steps of alchemical transformation is explained, with hands-on techniques and exercises, treating alchemy as a living discipline for achieving a spiritual awakening.”

title.rendered: Remember our Dreams

content.rendered:
Remember Our Dreams

Why did we start this in the first place? Did we start it for the money? Why did we want the money? The motivation behind our original plans can get lost quickly. Often, we have dreams of peace, free-time, a better future for our loved ones and us. Then, the steps we took to get there turn into empty routines that take us away from the very things we wanted to achieve in the first place. The second job, the fast-track to (future) success, and the overtime cause us to sacrifice a present for a promise someday and a future that doesn’t materialize.
Why did we start this in the first place? What did we originally want to do? Can we have it sooner? Sometimes the long road to peace isn’t necessary. Sometimes we can take the short cut and have it now. A shift in perspective; rather than a shift in our bank account can lead us to this peace.
What do we need to stop doing? What were the original dreams we had; and do our current activities match up with these dreams?
I once heard a speaker say that spiritual growth is a process of “uncover, discover, discard.” Let’s look at the things that aren’t fulfilling us and let them go. There needs to be a threshold of sacrifice that we aren’t willing to cross, no matter how exciting the pot of gold at the end of the rainbow may seem. A place to uncover is the routine or activity where we have to give ourselves multiple pep talks before we go. A true passion is something we look forward to; where we don’t to force it to go. We can then discover how we feel and why we feel that way. Do we need to discard our perspective and choose a more empowering conversation? Or do we need to discard the activity altogether? Connect with the original dream and motivation. The answer to happiness probably lies right where the path began.
